By Mitchell FermanOctober 29, 2026 at 7:06 AM UTCBookmark

Shell Plc reported the second-highest profit in its history on the back of record oil refining margins as the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict deprive the world of fuel-making capacity.
Adjusted net income surged to $10.8 billion in the third quarter, the London-based major said in an earnings statement on Thursday. That’s the highest since the three months immediately after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022. Analysts had anticipated a profit of $10.2 billion. Shell raised its share buyback to $5 billion and maintained its dividend.

A global rally in technology shares stalled after disappointing earnings from two industry heavyweights revived doubts over whether billions of dollars in AI spending will deliver sufficient returns.
Nasdaq 100 Index futures lost 1.1%, signaling that the underlying gauge’s three-day rally was set to end, while contracts for the S&P 500 Index dropped 0.3%. European shares were set for a tepid open. Asian equities declined 0.3%, with the Kospi Index sliding 1.2% in a sharp reversal after posting its biggest gain in three months on Wednesday.

Gold declined after the Federal Reserve kept borrowing costs steady and offered few clues on its next move, leaving open the prospect of a rate hike before year-end.
Bullion fell as much as 1.1% to near $4,020 an ounce, reversing three days of modest gains. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 in favor of holding interest rates steady, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank would likely reduce the number of rate decisions to six from eight per year — a move that analysts said could foster uncertainty.

Jio Platforms Ltd.’s sparkling debut was met with enthusiasm among investors, paving the way for more potential offerings by some of the country’s largest privately held companies.
The massive demand for Jio’s listing showed investors remain willing to commit significant capital to marquee deals, even against a difficult backdrop for Indian equities, according to investment bankers. The stock’s strong post-listing performance may also give prospective issuers greater confidence to press ahead with large transactions, they said.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Chinese tech hardware shares tumbled as impressive quarterly results at some companies failed to offset persistent concerns over fundamentals and weak global AI sentiment.
The chip-heavy STAR 50 Index dropped as much as 4.6% on Thursday after gaining 2.5% in the previous session. Artificial intelligence chipmaker Moore Threads Technology Co. plunged as much as 13% even after sales surged nearly 1,800% on-year in the three months through September. Memory chip producer Biwin Storage Technology Co. slid 14% after a more than 500% jump in profit.
